findings.title: Title art speaks a different visual language than the game
findings.where: Title screen — the full-bleed background matte sitting behind the SMDUEL logo and the menu panel.
findings.problem: The background is a soft, low-frequency painted matte (blurred clouds, painterly tanks, warm brown-orange film haze), while every other screen is hard-edged top-down sprites over a flat charcoal-and-cyan UI. The matte's warm palette shares no color with the game's signature teal-on-dark scheme except the logo itself, and the menu panel's cool cyan border floats on the warm painting without tying into it.
findings.why: On first load the player reads the splash as generic concept art bolted onto a different game, so the brand promise ('one car, sixteen cities') is never anchored to the look they are about to play; the abrupt style jump when entering New Driver makes the title feel like placeholder marketing art rather than part of the product.
findings.fix: Either replace the matte with an in-engine top-down shot (the orange car on the cracked-city ground under the same flat daylight as gameplay), or push the matte toward the game's palette — desaturate the oranges toward charcoal, add the HUD's cyan as rim-light on the tanks, and lay a faint scanline/vignette matching the menu panel — so title and gameplay share one color script.

findings.title: Lane markings run perpendicular to the car's heading
findings.where: Road screen — the two solid white lines and the dashed yellow centre line crossing the frame horizontally, versus the orange car in the centre pointing up.
findings.problem: The road's lane lines are drawn left-to-right (an east–west highway) but the player's car is oriented nose-up (north) on a north-up radar, i.e. broadside across the lanes. There are also no shoulders, barriers or road edges, so the grey asphalt fades into the same grey texture at top and bottom with no drivable boundary.
findings.why: At a glance the player cannot tell which way the road goes relative to their vehicle, and pressing W would drive the car off the pavement. The missing edges mean there is no readable corridor, so 'survive the highway' carries no visual stakes and the scene reads as a test pattern rather than a road.
findings.fix: Rotate the spawn heading (or the road texture and markings) so the car's long axis parallels the lane lines, and add defined road edges — a darker shoulder strip plus a guardrail or rumble-strip line on both sides — so the drivable corridor is bounded and the direction of travel is obvious the instant the screen appears.

findings.title: Stray magenta mount tabs break the car's silhouette
findings.where: Arena and Road screens — the small hot-pink rectangles protruding from the four corners and mid-sides of the orange car sprite.
findings.problem: The vehicle sprite is ringed with bright magenta nubs that stick out past the body outline; they look like debug hitboxes or unstyled empty sockets. In the constructor's top-view the same mount points are drawn as recessed teal slots flush inside the chassis, so the in-game render contradicts the build screen and reads as leftover developer geometry.
findings.why: Magenta is the loudest color on an otherwise muted screen, so the eye snaps to the car's edges instead of its shape or the arena; the protrusions make an otherwise finished-looking car appear unfinished and glitchy, undermining the 'build your car' payoff the constructor just sold.
findings.fix: Render empty mounts as dark recessed slots contained within the body silhouette (matching the constructor style), reserve magenta strictly for damage or invalid-fit feedback, and only show a colored mount graphic once a weapon or armour piece is actually installed.

findings.title: The city reads as an empty lot, and the gate is invisible
findings.where: City screen — the cracked-grey ground inside and outside the circular ring of building blocks, the scattered flat building sprites, and the perimeter ring itself.
findings.problem: There is no street grid, no sidewalks, no roads — just one uniform cracked-pavement texture filling the whole frame, with a handful of low-contrast white/cyan building decals scattered inside a haphazard circle of mismatched blocks. The instruction names 'the gate', but no opening in the perimeter ring is distinguished by shape, color or label, and the cyan objective chevron above the car points at empty pavement rather than an enterable building.
findings.why: The player cannot orient, cannot see where they are allowed to go, and cannot identify the two things the tutorial tells them to look for (a building, the gate); the world looks like a placeholder arena with props dropped in, killing the 'sixteen cities' atmosphere and turning navigation into guesswork.
findings.fix: Lay down an actual road network (darker asphalt strips with lane markings forming blocks) so buildings sit on lots beside streets; restyle the gate as a lit arched gap in the ring with its own accent color and an on-screen label; raise building contrast and scale and add a soft drop shadow so they read as structures; and snap the objective marker onto a real enterable doorway.

findings.title: Constructor is a flat spec sheet with a static, unlinked diagram
findings.where: Constructor screen — the left column of stat rows (five '0' armour rows and ten '(empty)' weapon rows) and the right 'SUBCOMPACT — TOP VIEW' outline.
findings.problem: Every left row has identical weight and styling, so the column reads as a monospace log with no grouping; meanwhile the top-view diagram never changes — selecting a Weapon or Armour row highlights nothing on the car, the side sockets stay empty teal rectangles, and the two interior blocks look the same regardless of build. The spec list and the car picture have no visual connection.
findings.why: The core fantasy of the game ('build a car') gets zero visual feedback; the player cannot see what they are attaching or where, so the screen feels like editing a config file rather than designing a vehicle, and the long wall of '(empty)' rows makes the build look broken or unfinished.
findings.fix: Group the left list under accented section headers (CHASSIS / ARMOUR / WEAPONS) with dividers, dim empty slots as ghost outlines that visibly fill when set, and wire the diagram to the selection: highlight the matching socket or edge on the top-view when a row is focused, and draw mounted armour as colored plates on the chassis edges and weapons as icons in their sockets so the car updates live as you build.
